feedback.problem:
Compute the volume $V$ of the parallelepiped spanned by the vectors $a=⟨1,2,3⟩$, $b=⟨0,5,0⟩$, and $c=⟨4,0,6⟩.$

$V=${{field-1}}
feedback.worked_solution:
The volume of a parallelepiped spanned by three vectors is given by the absolute value of their triple product.

First, we compute the triple product:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & 6\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & 6\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 4 & 6\end{aligned}|+3\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 5 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(30)-2(0)+3(-20) \\  & =30-0-60 \\  & =-30\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the absolute value. So, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped is 

$$
V=|-30|=30.
$$
